narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 36.0%. That is not a certainty of default, but it was above the lender’s approval cutoff, so the application was denied. The most influential factor was the length of the requested loan: at 8 months, well below the approved-applicant average of about 19 months, it pushed the decision toward good credit. The next most important factor was your checking-account status. Because it was below zero, a situation seen for only 12.6% of approved applicants, it pushed strongly toward bad credit and was the main warning sign. Your credit history—rated as critical/other credits—was the third most important factor and, in this case, leaned toward good credit, although it was a smaller influence than the other two. To improve a future application, focus first on the account issue: bring the checking account into positive balance, avoid overdrafts, and provide recent statements showing stable balances. Also review the critical/other credit entries, settle or document them, and ask the lender what additional evidence would support approval. A shorter loan request helped you; maintaining cleaner account and credit records should strengthen your next application.
